summary.headline: S H Kelkar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore, with EBITDA up 21% to Rs 89 crore and margin at 13.4%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore and EBITDA rose 21% to Rs 89 crore, with margin expanding to 13.4% from 12.6%. Flavours was the standout, at Rs 112 crore, which management says includes about Rs 15 crore of one-off pre-ordering and stock build; the normalised run-rate is about Rs 95-96 crore. Global Ingredients was softer on supply gaps, and Fragrances India was flat as the company exited low-margin business and repriced clients. Net debt rose Rs 65 crore to Rs 852 crore on inventory build and capex, and a Rs 30 crore insurance exceptional item was booked.

financial_highlights.change: Supported by product mix and raw material planning
Normalised about Rs 95-96 crore excluding about Rs 15 crore pre-ordering
Expected to rise to Rs 38-39 crore per quarter after Vanvate capitalisation

segments.name: Flavours
segments.commentary: Strong broad-based growth; Rs 112 crore in Q1 versus a normalised Rs 95-96 crore, with about Rs 15 crore attributed to pre-ordering and extra channel stock. Management expects Q2 to be above Rs 95-96 crore but not above Rs 112 crore.

segments.name: Fragrances (Europe and international)
segments.commentary: Healthy growth led by Europe and select international markets. Europe plant operational since May; European capex completed. Segment margins are weighed down by higher R&D and global CDC opex.

segments.name: Fragrances India
segments.commentary: Flat YoY, against a strong Q1 FY26 base. Company exited low-margin business and held back shipments until price corrections were agreed; about 95% of clients accepted price increases.

segments.name: Global Ingredients
segments.commentary: Softer quarter on lower demand in select export markets and supply gaps from raw-material constraints; management expects recovery in H2.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit revenue growth and improved margins for full FY27, but would not give a precise full-year margin range beyond the next 2-3 months.
If double-digit growth holds, EBITDA in absolute terms should be similar to Q1 levels; margin could vary about 1% either way.
Raw material costs said to be fixed for about 6 months via stock in hand and contracts; about 45 days extra inventory built to pass on future cost shocks.
Net debt expected broadly flat at June level through Q2 (may rise slightly in September), then fall about Rs 25 crore per quarter from Q3.
Remaining India capex about Rs 100 crore in total (Rs 25 crore in Q1 done, Rs 25 crore in Q2 on Vanvate, about Rs 50 crore for the three India plants); Vanvate factory commissioning in Q3.
Long-term targets: ROCE above 15% in 3-5 years and 20% long term; European business ROCE 17-18% over the long run.
US revenue expected at about USD 1.5-2 million for FY27; UK business needs 12-15 months before material revenue.
capex_capacity: Europe capex of about Rs 25 crore in Q1 completed; Almere factory operational since May 2026 and a large R&D centre in Germany added.
India: Vanvate factory to be commissioned in Q3 FY27; bulk of India investment capex expected by end of Q2.
Vashivali plant upgrade: last Rs 25 crore may be spent in Q4 FY27 or deferred to Q1 FY28, depending on demand.
Extra R&D spend of about USD 3 million a year in Europe.
Quarterly depreciation about Rs 35 crore, rising to Rs 38-39 crore after Vanvate capitalisation.
demand_pricing: Price corrections passed to about 95%+ of clients after raw-material cost inflation linked to West Asia geopolitics; clients reluctant to accept were not supplied until negotiations concluded.
Flavours pre-ordering of 1-2 to 3 weeks was driven by long lead and shipping times; July momentum reported as steady.
Global Ingredients supply curtailed due to raw-material uncertainty; backward integration and China de-risking steps said to be in place.
Unilever and global accounts: ongoing project flow but no large new breakthroughs; Unilever's own pricing pressures and weak India launches noted.
Management cites a US plus UK fragrance market of about USD 10 billion, roughly 4-5x India's fragrance market, with about USD 100 million addressable in the near term.
Around 10-11% of revenue comes from products launched in the last 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year Flavours budget and how much did FX add to revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Flavours was Rs 112 crore versus a normalised Rs 95-96 crore, with about Rs 15 crore pulled forward. Like-for-like growth was about 9%, and FX added about 5 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Is flat India Fragrance a high-base effect, and what is the trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 was strong. The company deliberately exited low-margin business, held back shipments during price negotiations, and says it now services almost all clients after building inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be guided for FY27, and is the Q1 gross margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise full-year range was given. Management says Q1 is a normal quarter, not exceptional, so EBITDA should be similar in absolute terms if double-digit growth continues, with margin varying about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the factory timelines, debt path and tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Vanvate commissions in Q3. Debt stays near June levels, then falls about Rs 25 crore a quarter from Q3. ETR is 31.5-32% now, targeted below 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Europe ramp-up and return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Germany is expected to break even in FY27 or FY28, the US a year later, and the UK a year after that. Long-term European ROCE is 17-18%, and group ROCE above 15% in 3-5 years, rising to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the insurance claim status and how is depreciation trending?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 30 crore was received in Q1, with Rs 50-60 crore still pending and full settlement expected in FY27. Depreciation is about Rs 35 crore a quarter, rising to Rs 38-39 crore after Vanvate.

risks_watch: Flavours Q1 (Rs 112 crore) includes about Rs 15 crore of pre-ordering and extra channel stock that management says will not recur every quarter; Q2 is guided above Rs 95-96 crore but not above Rs 112 crore

Raw material cost visibility of about 6 months from July, backed by stock in hand, contracts and about 45 days of extra inventory; cost shocks beyond that could hit gross margin if prices cannot be passed on
Global Ingredients softness from supply gaps and lower export demand; recovery is expected only in H2 FY27
Fragrances India flat YoY after deliberate exit from low-margin business and shipment holds; watch whether volumes recover as price increases settle

Net debt of Rs 852 crore expected to stay near June level through Q2 (may rise in September), with reduction of about Rs 25 crore per quarter only from Q3; Rs 50-60 crore of insurance claim still pending

Europe and India capex ramp: Vanvate commissioning in Q3 FY27, Europe losses expected to persist until breakeven in FY27-FY28 (Germany), with US and UK following a year apart; effective tax rate is 31.5-32% against a target below 30%
key_quotes: So, we have prepared in a manner that we have 6 months visibility on the inventory and our contracts or pricing to the client.
But for the full year, we are not confident to predict beyond 2, 3 months' time.
This is the baseline normal quarter.
We do not expect Rs. 112 plus growth in the quarter 2. That is not our expectation.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and guarded on the outlook: management calls Q1 a normal quarter but declines to give a full-year margin range beyond 2-3 months, citing geopolitical volatility, energy and freight costs. Confident on near-term execution points such as raw material cover, Europe plant commissioning and supply continuity for existing clients.
